title: AJ Cooper is the Co-Founder and CEO of Itera
gist: Itera CEO AJ Cooper pitches a 'fluid' circuit board that uses liquid metal on glass and electrowetting to rewire itself in under a minute, aiming to collapse months of PCB validation cycles into days via a remote electronics-as-a-service model. He says a top 5 global auto OEM and defense neoprimes have reserved production capacity.

insights.claim: Itera's 'fluid' circuit board replaces etched copper with liquid metal on glass substrates and uses electrowetting so traces can be redrawn to match a new design in under a minute.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: If it works at scale, the physical interconnect becomes programmable like chips and software.
insights.quote: the fluid board uses liquid metal on glass substrates

insights.claim: Itera likens its board to e-paper: each pixel is either metal or not and holds state with power off because microscopic structures retain the metal, so engineers test real components with real electrical behavior rather than simulation.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Real-component testing is the claimed differentiator versus simulation.

insights.claim: Any internal node on the fluid board can be probed, giving far more observability than a traditional PCB.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Observability could shorten debug time beyond the reconfiguration speed.

insights.claim: Cooper argues that electronics are programmable everywhere except the physical interconnect, and that Itera's process innovation is the foundation for hardware that can change itself after deployment.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Signals a roadmap from validation tool to field-reconfigurable hardware, still unproven.
insights.quote: Electronics are programmable everywhere except for the physical interconnect
insights.locator: What new features/technology are you working on?

insights.claim: Traditional prototyping sends designs to an overseas fab house, waits weeks, finds a flaw and repeats; Cooper says lucky teams do 3 cycles but veterans have lived through 6-10 before production.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Each spin costs weeks, so validation is a major hidden schedule and cost driver.

insights.claim: Itera claims it compresses a months-long validation process into days, and potentially faster with an AI-assisted EDA tool, reducing the cost of being wrong to zero.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Pairing with AI EDA could make iteration speed the limiting factor of hardware development.
insights.locator: Our board compresses a months-long process into days

insights.claim: Cooper sizes the addressable market at about $50 billion spent annually on hardware development and validation.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.locator: What application areas are your strongest?

insights.claim: Cooper frames the competition as only traditional PCB fabrication (weeks per iteration) and simulation (fast but unable to capture real component behavior), claiming Itera closes the gap between testing accuracy and iteration speed with no direct fluid-circuit competitor.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: A new-category claim; validity depends on whether customers accept fluid-board fidelity as real.
insights.locator: What does the competitive landscape look like

insights.claim: Itera operates secure U.S.-based testing centers where customers get remote access to a 'Configurable Twin' of their board rather than buying hardware.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: A service model avoids selling capital equipment and keeps the technology in-house.

insights.claim: Customers upload the same files they would send to a PCB manufacturer and get remote access via existing IDEs and interfaces (UART, USB, Ethernet, SD card, camera), designed for zero adoption friction.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Compatibility with existing EDA flows lowers switching cost.

insights.claim: Cooper says a top 5 global auto OEM and defense neoprimes have reserved Itera's production capacity and that it is talking to hyperscalers and chipset manufacturers.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Unnamed customer claims offer early commercial validation but cannot be checked.
insights.locator: What application areas are your strongest?
